name: occupation-lookup
description:
Type-ahead over the 6363-row occupation reference table, for the quote form's
occupation field (plan A-06). Gateway-mapped so the browser can POST to it.

Payload:
```json
{ "query": "physio", "product": "itpi", "eligibility": "yes,refer", "limit": 25, "offset": 0 }
```

- `query` is prefix-matched per whitespace token against occupation_label and
  lowercased first (the index stores lowercase prefixes; "PHYS" matches nothing).
  Multiple tokens are ANDed, so "software dev" means "a word starting with
  software AND a word starting with dev", in any order.
- `product` is one of itpi | ah / allied_health | gp / general_property. It adds
  an OR group over the three-valued <product>_eligibility field. `eligibility`
  overrides the values wanted (default "yes,refer" = quotable). The index has no
  negation, so "quotable" is always an OR of the wanted values, never "not no".
- `limit` defaults to 25 and is capped at 50; `offset` pages. Results are sorted
  by occupation_label (a text_sortable index field) so paging is stable.
- Below the 3-character minimum, and with no product to browse by, PREPARE
  substitutes a sentinel keyword filter that matches nothing: the flow returns an
  empty page rather than scanning, and `reason` says why.
- Never issues an unbounded read: limit is always set and always <= 50.

Returns `{options:[{value,text,note,...}], total, count, limit, offset, has_more,
next_offset, reason, searched}`. `value` is occupation_code, `text` is
occupation_label. Prefill keys sit at the TOP LEVEL of each row because
lookup.utils.prefillWrites indexes the row flatly.
